Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks to the Press
Remarks
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
Joint Base Andrews
October 17, 2026
QUESTION:
Mr. Secretary?
SECRETARY RUBIO:
What’s going on?
QUESTION:
Nice and chilly, right?
SECRETARY RUBIO:
It’s all right.
QUESTION:
With everything going on in the world and with crisis all over, why are you choosing now, at this time, to go to Uzbekistan?
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Well, it’s the time of year that worked for those leaders.  It’s not just Uzbekistan, it’s the other four countries from Central Asia.  This is an important relationship.  I mean, one of the things that suffers is the strategic business.  You’re always visiting someplace where there’s a crisis or there’s a problem or there’s a – you’re going because there’s a conference.  But there’s countries you’d like to get to because we want to build our relationships with them.  And so that’s what we did a couple weeks ago when we went to Greece and other places like that, and earlier, a few weeks earlier than that, we went to Latin America, and now to Central Asia.  So – and the chance to see – it was the date that worked to get all five of the leaders together, all five of the foreign ministers from the five countries.
QUESTION:
On Starshield, what’s going on?  Because Elon Musk said it’s up to the President.
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Well, Starshield or Starlink?
QUESTION:
Well, just both.
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Yeah, I know, it’s confusing.  So Starlink is a commercial product, okay?  And so they – it’s regulated and handled as a commercial product.  Starshield is a defense product, a military product.  And as I said, I mean, that is something that we have a military – the United States military uses.  It’s not at this moment available to Ukraine, and that’s under conversation.  It’s under discussion right now of how they would want to use it.
QUESTION:
No, but did the U.S. – did the U.S. have anything to do with it not working in Ukraine?  Zelenskyy said it was deliberate.
SECRETARY RUBIO:
No.  Well, I don’t know what Zelenskyy said.  I’m not sure Zelenskyy knows what he’s talking about, but it wasn’t deliberate.  We have nothing to do with that.  I don’t – the United States, nobody ordered that Starlink speed to be slowed down.  It sort of happened, but my understanding is it’s been restored.  It’s back to where it was before.  That’s Starlink, though.  They were using Starlink for their drones.
QUESTION:
Has Starshield been restored?
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Starshield is a totally different product.  Starshield is –
QUESTION:
I know, but is it –
SECRETARY RUBIO:
No, no, Starshield is a contract with the U.S. military.  It has nothing to do with Ukraine.  I know Ukraine wants access to Starshield.  They do not have Starshield now.  They’ve asked for access to it in order to conduct deep strikes inside of Russia.  They do not have access to it at this moment.  Those are two different products.
QUESTION:
But you have to have a theory as to why, obviously, Ukraine has reported disruptions.
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Yeah, I don’t know what their theory is, but nothing to do with the White House.  I saw a report on that the other day.  It’s just categorically false.  No one at the White House ordered anyone to slow down internet or slow down speed so that certain drones couldn’t use it.  But my understanding is it’s back up and running.  That’s what I read – that’s what we heard two days ago.
QUESTION:
Sir, on the sanctions waivers on Russia.  Senator Ted Cruz today called it a big mistake that only serves to benefit Putin.  I’m wondering what your response is to that.
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Well, there are other countries – the problem is these sanctions were not just sanctions on Russia.  They include tariffs on a number of countries – India, for example, and others.  And so I think the President wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyze what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the U.S. economy.  I think when the bill was passed, one of the reasons the waivers were put in there is understanding that they would need some period of time to study this, given all the different things that are going on in the world right now, including the pressure on global energy supplies that are happening not just because of Iran, not just because of the Straits of Hormuz, but increasingly because of the Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia and because of the war with Ukraine and Russia, where energy infrastructure is being hit.  And so that’s having an impact on global prices as well.
So, I think you have to take all of that into account and weigh it against each other.  And then you’ve got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it’s hard to pivot from one day to the next, but they’re also an important ally and partner of the United States.  So, the President – we need that period of time to sort of study all this and figure out what the right combination is.
QUESTION:
Between this waiver and the diesel deal, I mean, there’s a criticism that you’re basically giving Putin something for nothing, we’re giving Putin these freebies.  What’s your response?
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Well, that diesel was going to be sold one way or the other.  I mean, the diesel that Putin is going to sell, they would make it available to the global market one way or the other.  The only difference is how much of it the United States was going to get.  So – but this is not unprecedented.  If you recall a few months ago, we also did a 60-day waiver on Russian oil when Hormuz was being challenged.
So yeah, these conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other, and they’re having an impact not just on global oil and diesel prices, but on economics.  And I mean, the United States, we’re paying higher prices than we all want to be paying, but you look at some of these other countries around the world, they’re near crisis mode.  So, all of these things have to be managed delicately and worked with because they’re all – they’re all coming together now.  It’s not just the Strait of Hormuz anymore.  It’s what’s happening with Saudi Arabia and the uncertainty that that’s creating.  It’s also what’s happening between Russia and Ukraine and the constraints that’s putting on global energy supplies.
QUESTION:
I’d like to ask you about violence in the West Bank.  My colleague, Heidi Levine, was attacked there yesterday.
SECRETARY RUBIO:
I saw that.  We’re all – we’re very disturbed by those images and what we’re seeing.  We’ve asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff.  That – the President’s been very clear.  He’s said this repeatedly.  He does not want to see friction or anything, a crisis, going on in the West Bank.  Now, I understand that these are groups that are out there doing it, and the President has been repeatedly clear when he’s said that he doesn’t want to see that.  He doesn’t want to see a new spark.
But we saw the reports about what happened yesterday.  I don’t have all the details.  I only go off media reports.  I know we’ve inquired with the embassy, are supposed to get a cable back later today or tomorrow indicating exactly what they know about it.  But from what I understand about media reports, it didn’t look good.  It was an American reporter; there was a photo of a journalist who was caught behind where some of these groups came in and was beaten.  There’s video of that.  So look, the whole thing was just disturbing and didn’t – not a good look.
QUESTION:
Mr. Secretary, the President, one of the first decisions he took was to lift sanctions against the settlers.
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Yeah, I understand, but he doesn’t want to see what’s happening now.
QUESTION:
No, that’s not –
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Lifting sanctions, which he did earlier in the day, does not mean he’s a supporter of what he’s seeing now on television, what he’s reading about.  We’d like to get all the facts and learn a little bit more about it, but that – look, that’s one instance, and it happened to involve a photojournalist.  But there are other instances we’ve had complaints about.  Now it’s this olive harvest season, and so traditionally that’s always been a time in which a lot of people come into those areas.  So, we’ve been watching that closely.  We know that’s an issue there, that’s potentially an issue in Lebanon as well.  Okay?
QUESTION:
Do you agree with the UK assessment, the intel assessment that Russia and Iran may be increasing hybrid attacks over the next few months?
SECRETARY RUBIO:
But which assessment are you talking about?
QUESTION:
The – both NATO and UK have indicated –
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Oh, NATO.
QUESTION:
Have indicated that in –
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Yeah, but those are two separate things.  So in the case of – you’re asking about Russian hybrid attacks.  Yeah, we’ve always been concerned that the war in Ukraine can metastasize into other parts of Europe and other parts of the world, whether it be sabotage operations or the like.  We’ve always been concerned that that’s one of the risks of a stalemated conflict, is escalation, and escalation can take the form of irregular attacks or irregular events.  So that’s something I raised a couple weeks ago and we’re watching that closely.
I think with Iran and UK, what the UK has said is that the Iranians were behind the plot to attack the air base.  And obviously we have no reason to disagree with the assessment factually.  In fact, we agree with it.
So, all right?  It’s cold, guys.
QUESTION:
On the case regarding my colleague, what’s –
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Did you guys see my Gators today take down Texas on the road?
Go ahead.
QUESTION:
The case regarding my colleague who was attacked in the West Bank, what steps will you take to ensure that there’s a proper investigation of this incident?
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Well, we want to learn all the facts about it first.  Obviously, we’ve seen the video, and we’ve seen the media reporting about it.  We have a process to handle these sorts of things.  And if, in fact, it turns out to be what it appears it was, then we have ways of communicating that to the Israelis about how we expect – that we would expect them to prevent that from happening in the future.  And it’s – again, the President doesn’t want to see a crisis in the West Bank.  We don’t need that right now.  Israel doesn’t need that right now.
QUESTION:
Can I ask briefly on Eritrea-Ethiopia?
SECRETARY RUBIO:
Yeah.
QUESTION:
How high-risk is the chance of war between them?  And do you feel like it was a mistake to lift some of those Ethiopia-related sanctions right before violence flared up?
SECRETARY RUBIO:
No, I don’t think those – I don’t – no, I don’t think the sanctions lifting – these were very small sanctions, and they don’t really have anything to do with what’s happening over there.  You have these separatists that were attacking inside of Ethiopia.  You had an Ethiopian response to it.  You see troops surging on both sides of the border as a result of that.  And anytime you see troops on both sides of the border in a place like that, you’re always worried that that can turn into a broader conflict.
So, we don’t have the closest relationship with Eritrea, obviously, over the years, although we’ve had communication with them – more than usual – in the past few months.  Our hope was that by lifting some of these sanctions, we can increase those links because it’s hard to serve the role of mediator and peacemaker unless you can talk to both sides.
Obviously, the Ethiopian side we talk to a lot more, and I spoke to them this week personally, a few days ago, and just reiterated how important it was – like, we understand the challenge you’re facing from these separatists, and obviously no one is supportive of terrorism and the terrorist attacks that came against them – drone attacks against their own capital – but we also think we – it’s a time to sort of be wise and measured in how you respond to that and make sure it doesn’t turn into a broader war which could ultimately pull in other countries.  The last thing the world needs right now is another war.
Okay?  Thank you, guys.
